ucs.title: [LLM] TA505 (Clop / Spandex Tempest) Get2/MSI downloader: Office or script host spawning msiexec/rundll32 to a remote URL
ucs.description: Hunts TA505's signature initial-access-to-install chain where a weaponized Excel/HTML-smuggling attachment causes Office (or wscript/mshta) to launch msiexec or rundll32 against a remote payload URL — the delivery mechanism for the Get2 downloader and SDBbot RAT that precede Clop ransomware. This combination of a productivity/script-host parent invoking a LOLBin with an inline http(s) argument is characteristic of TA505 malspam loaders rather than benign software installs.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=msiexec.exe OR Processes.process_name=rundll32.exe) AND (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","explorer.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*http://*" OR Processes.process="*https://*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_id
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| where user!="*$"
| sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("msiexec.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","explorer.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://")          // remote payload retrieval, not a local MSI
| where AccountName !endswith "$"                                   // exclude machine/SYSTEM context
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("msiexec.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","explorer.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'

    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\winword.exe'
      - '\excel.exe'
      - '\powerpnt.exe'
      - '\outlook.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\explorer.exe'
  selection_url:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate web-hosted MSI deployments invoked from a browser/explorer context
level: high
tags:

  - attack.t1218.007
  - attack.t1218.011
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.g0092

ucs.title: [LLM] TA505 Clop ransomware mass-encryption: .Clop extension fan-out and ClopReadMe ransom-note drops
ucs.description: Detects the impact stage of a TA505 intrusion: a single process renaming/creating large numbers of files with the .Clop / .C_L_O_P extension and dropping the 'ClopReadMe.txt' / 'README_README.txt' ransom note. Clop is TA505's signature ransomware and its fixed extension and note filenames are a strong actor fingerprint.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as file_names values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="*.Clop" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.C_L_O_P" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.CIop" OR Filesystem.file_name="ClopReadMe.txt" OR Filesystem.file_name="README_README.txt" OR Filesystem.file_name="!_READ_ME.RTF") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| stats dc(file_name) as distinct_files values(file_names) as sample_files min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime by dest process_id
| where distinct_files > 50
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - distinct_files
ucs.kql:
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".Clop"
    or FileName endswith ".C_L_O_P"
    or FileName endswith ".CIop"
    or FileName in~ ("ClopReadMe.txt","README_README.txt","!_READ_ME.RTF")
| summarize EncryptedFiles = dcount(FolderPath),
            SampleFiles   = make_set(FileName, 8),
            FirstSeen     = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen      = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
             InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where EncryptedFiles > 50      // 50 = mass-encryption floor; benign renamers rarely touch this many distinct paths/process
| order by EncryptedFiles desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("Clop","C_L_O_P","CIop")
    or TargetFileName in~ ("ClopReadMe.txt","README_README.txt","!_READ_ME.RTF")
| summarize EncryptedFiles = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            SampleFiles   = make_set(TargetFileName, 8),
            FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessId
| where EncryptedFiles > 50
| order by EncryptedFiles desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Clop Ransomware File Extension and Ransom Note (TA505)
id: a91c7d52-44be-4e1f-bd3a-ta505clopfs02
status: experimental
description: Detects Clop ransomware encrypting files with the .Clop extension or dropping its ransom notes, the impact stage of a TA505 intrusion.
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.Clop'
      - '.C_L_O_P'
      - '.CIop'
  selection_note:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\ClopReadMe.txt'
      - '\README_README.txt'
      - '\!_READ_ME.RTF'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Security tooling staging quarantined samples with these names
level: critical
tags:
  - attack.actions
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1486
  - attack.g0092
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*.Clop OR *.clop OR *.C_L_O_P OR *.CIop) OR @TargetFilename:(*\ClopReadMe.txt OR *\README_README.txt OR *\!_READ_ME.RTF))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/(\.clop$|\.c_l_o_p$|\.ciop$|\\clopreadme\.txt$|\\readme_readme\.txt$|\\!_read_me\.rtf$)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=encrypted_files))
| encrypted_files > 50
ucs.rationale: Clop is the ransomware family MITRE and CrowdStrike attribute directly to TA505 (G0092), and the '.Clop' file extension plus 'ClopReadMe.txt'/'README_README.txt' note filenames are hard-coded, family-specific indicators rather than generic ransomware behaviour.
